Political developments after 1975

After the Navnirman period, Gujarat experienced further changes of government and political leadership. Some Chief Ministers returned to office after an interval, while others are remembered for important electoral or political milestones.

The chronology below identifies major completed tenures and the basic facts needed to distinguish leaders. It is not a list of current office-holders.

PeriodChief MinisterMain fact
1975–1976; 1977–1980Babubhai J. PatelServed in 2 separate periods
1976–1977; 1980–1985; 1989–1990Madhavsinh SolankiHeld office in multiple periods
1985–1989Amarsinh ChaudharyFirst Chief Minister from a Scheduled Tribe community
1990–1994Chimanbhai PatelReturned to office after his 1973–1974 tenure
1994–1995Chhabildas MehtaSucceeded Chimanbhai Patel
1995; 1998–2001Keshubhai PatelLed the BJP government formed in 1995; later returned
1995–1996Suresh MehtaSucceeded Keshubhai Patel's first ministry
1996–1997Shankersinh VaghelaLed a ministry after the 1996 political change
1997–1998Dilip ParikhSucceeded Shankersinh Vaghela
After 2000Chief Minister's officeHeads the state Council of Ministers
2014–2016Anandiben PatelFirst woman Chief Minister of Gujarat
After 2000Chief Minister's officeThe ministry must retain the Assembly's confidence

The 1980s: Madhavsinh Solanki and Amarsinh Chaudhary

Madhavsinh Solanki was a prominent Congress leader associated with Gujarat politics in the 1980s. His electoral strategy became associated with the KHAM social coalition: Kshatriya, Harijan, Adivasi and Muslim. The word 'Harijan' is retained here only as part of the historical name of that political formula; Scheduled Castes is the appropriate constitutional term.

Amarsinh Chaudhary became Chief Minister in July 1985 and is remembered as Gujarat's first Chief Minister from a Scheduled Tribe community.

The political and reservation-related agitations of the 1980s must not be confused with the Navnirman Movement of 1974, whose immediate causes were rising prices and corruption.

The 1990s: changing parties and governments

Chimanbhai Patel returned as Chief Minister in 1990. His return demonstrates why a person's first and later terms should be treated separately when interpreting a chronological question.

In 1995, the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) formed a government under Keshubhai Patel after winning the Gujarat Assembly election. Keshubhai later served another term beginning in 1998. The intervening period included ministries headed by Suresh Mehta, Shankersinh Vaghela and Dilip Parikh.

Chief-Minister milestones after 2000

The Chief Minister heads the state government, and the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Legislative Assembly.

Anandiben Patel took office on 22 May 2014 and became the first woman Chief Minister of Gujarat. Successive Chief Ministers are appointed by the Governor and must command the confidence of the Legislative Assembly.

Connecting the main dates across the subtopic

The broad sequence is straightforward: the Mahagujarat demand grew during the bilingual Bombay arrangement in the 1950s; Gujarat was formed in 1960; important state institutions and reforms developed in the early 1960s; the capital shifted in 1970; Navnirman changed Gujarat politics in 1974–1975; the 1993 Panchayats Act renewed the statutory framework for rural local government; the BJP formed a government in 1995; and Gujarat's first woman Chief Minister assumed office in 2014.

Prelims focus

  • Babubhai J. Patel served in more than 1 period.
  • Madhavsinh Solanki was associated with the KHAM political formula.
  • Amarsinh Chaudhary became the first Chief Minister from a Scheduled Tribe community in 1985.
  • Chimanbhai Patel returned as Chief Minister in 1990.
  • Keshubhai Patel headed the BJP government formed in 1995.
  • The Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Legislative Assembly.
  • Anandiben Patel became Gujarat's first woman Chief Minister in 2014.
  • Trap: The first woman Chief Minister and the first Chief Minister from a Scheduled Tribe community are different historical distinctions.

[Historical chief-minister tenure compilation, All Gujarat News, 27 July 2022; Times of India, 'Movements That Shaped Davids and Goliaths of Gujarat Politics,' 27 November 2022; Indian Express, 'Gujarat Assembly Elections 2017: Quotas, Asmita, and How the Battle This Year Has Come Full Circle,' 18 December 2017; Indian Express, 'Anandiben Patel Is Gujarat's First Woman Chief Minister,' 23 May 2014; Lok Sabha Secretariat, Journal of Parliamentary Information, December 2021, 'Gujarat' section recording the September 2021 resignation; Bombay Reorganisation Act, 1960, sections 2–3; Ahmedabad District Administration, Government of Gujarat, 'History'; Government of Gujarat, Gujarat Panchayats Act, 1993. Online sources consulted 23 November 2026.]

title: Later Chief-Minister Milestones and the Main Political Turning Points
